intro.title: About University Square
intro.description: Piața Universității is one of the most historically significant squares in Bucharest, and an important symbol of the 1989 Romanian Revolution. The square is surrounded by important buildings including the University of Bucharest and the former National Library, making it an excellent place to experience Romanian history and culture.

Square is open 24 hours, can visit anytime

transport.title: Transportation
transport.metroDesc: Universitate Station (M2 Line), about 2 mins walk
transport.walkDesc: About 10-15 mins walk from the city center
transport.airportDesc: Direct metro or taxi from Bucharest Airport, approx. 20-30 mins.
transport.selfDriveDesc: Paid parking available nearby, but city center spots are limited
transport.intercityDesc: About 3km from North Railway Station, accessible by metro
transport.cyclingDesc: Public bicycle parking spots are available around the square
transport.tipsDesc: The square is located in the city center with convenient public transport. Walking or taking the metro is recommended.

route.title: Recommended Route
route.overview: Recommended to visit in the evening, starting from University Square, visiting Revolution Monument, former National Library, National Theatre, Athenaeum Square in sequence. The whole walk is relaxing and easy. Standard visit takes 30 minutes to 1 hour.
steps: Arrive at University Square Metro Station, walk to the center of the square
Visit the Revolution Monument and sculpture group, learn about 1989 Revolution history
Stroll to the former National Library building, admire the building exterior
Head to nearby Bucharest National Theatre
Relax at nearby cafés, feel the relaxed atmosphere of Bucharest
If time permits, visit nearby museums or shopping malls
Return via the original route or continue exploring nearby attractions
supplements: Square is open all day, evening lights are highly recommended.
Many cafes and restaurants around for resting.
Keep personal belongings safe in crowded areas.
Combine visit with nearby attractions (National Theatre, Athenaeum, etc.)
Some areas might be temporarily closed during major public events. Check ahead.

sections.title: 1989 Romanian Revolution
sections.content: University Square was one of the central locations during the 1989 Romanian Revolution. It was here that students and citizens gathered to protest against the communist regime, making it a powerful symbol of freedom and democracy for the Romanian people.

sections.title: Architectural Significance
sections.content: The square is surrounded by architectural landmarks, including the main building of the University of Bucharest, the National Theatre, and the InterContinental Hotel. The juxtaposition of neoclassical and modern architecture reflects the city's complex history.

sections.title: Cultural Hub
sections.content: Today, University Square remains a vibrant cultural hub. It frequently hosts open-air concerts, seasonal markets, and public gatherings. The nearby streets of the Old Town offer a glimpse into the bustling social life of Bucharest.
